evals.prompt: Our Dune app does not have COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN set. Use TyGen to generate client helpers for the EquipmentModel.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply TyGen or enable the flag. Explain that TyGen is an opt-in alpha capability and continue with the native @cognite/sdk APIs and types already used by the app.

assertions.text: Response requires COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN to be explicitly true before TyGen is used.
Response does not add or enable the alpha flag.
Response recommends the native @cognite/sdk as the fallback.

evals.prompt: COGNITE_ALPHA_ENABLE_TYGEN=true is already set for this app. Generate types for the data model production:EquipmentModel:v3 using the default output location.
evals.expected_output: Run cognite tygen generate with the versioned --data-model value and explain that the default output directory is src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/. The explicit generation request is sufficient confirmation.

assertions.text: Response uses cognite tygen generate rather than apps sdk types.
Response accepts the explicit generation request as confirmation and does not ask for redundant permission.
Response passes --data-model production:EquipmentModel:v3.
Response identifies src/generated_types/EquipmentModel as the default output directory.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled and the app uses the typed query build of the CLI. What files will generation create, and how do I read a work order's name with a type-checked query instead of untyped instances.query?
evals.expected_output: State that generation creates types.ts, views.ts and query.ts. Explain that query.ts exports initTygen, that tygen.query takes a native instances.query request written inline, and that the selected properties are typed in the result. search, aggregate and list stay on the native @cognite/sdk.

assertions.text: Response names types.ts, views.ts and query.ts.
Response binds the client once with initTygen and calls tygen.query with the request.
The query nests the generated view reference inside sources: [{ source: ..., properties: [...] }] and reads the result by space and externalId/version.
Response keeps instances.search, aggregate and list on the native @cognite/sdk.

evals.prompt: We changed a CDF data model after TyGen generation. Should I edit src/generated_types/EquipmentModel/types.ts to add the new field?
evals.expected_output: Regenerate from the versioned data model, inspect the generated diff, run typecheck and relevant tests, and commit the generated output with the app source. Do not hand-edit generated files.

assertions.text: Response instructs regeneration instead of hand-editing generated files.
Response requires inspecting the generated diff.
Response requires typecheck and relevant tests.
Response says to commit the generated output with the app source.

evals.prompt: The TyGen alpha flag is enabled. I want to generate types but do not know the data model reference. I can use an interactive terminal and browser login. How should I run TyGen?
evals.expected_output: Run tygen generate without --data-model in an interactive terminal so the model picker selects a versioned model. Use --interactive for browser authentication and explain that it is independent of the model picker.

assertions.text: Response omits --data-model to use the interactive model picker.
Response uses --interactive for browser authentication and distinguishes it from the model picker.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. Write a typed query for the Equipment view in the generated PlantModel types: only equipment whose status is 'RUNNING', sorted by name ascending, 25 at a time.
evals.expected_output: Use tygen.query with the request written inline. The filter and sort paths use [space, 'Equipment/version', property] and the select lists the properties that are read. The limit is 25.

assertions.text: Response uses initTygen and tygen.query rather than untyped instances.query.
Filter and sort property paths have the form [space, 'View/version', property] with literal strings.
The request is written inline or kept in a variable with as const satisfies QueryInput.
Response sets limit: 25 and a sort on name.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. I build the status filter in a helper function that takes a status string and returns the filter, and sometimes I add it to the query conditionally. The typed query now rejects it. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Explain that a property path only keeps its literal type when it is written inside the request, so the helper should return QueryFilter (or use as const), and the conditional part can be spread into the and array.

assertions.text: Response gives the helper a QueryFilter return type or as const.
Response explains that the literal type is lost when the path is built outside the request.
Response does not suggest casting the path to string[] or any.

evals.prompt: TyGen alpha is enabled. Add a 'load more' button to a typed query by passing the cursor from the previous response, when there is one.
evals.expected_output: Spread the cursor into the request only when it is set: ...(cursor ? { cursors: { equipment: cursor } } : {}). Do not write cursors: cursor ? {...} : {}, which loses the result types, or : undefined, which fails with exactOptionalPropertyTypes. Read the next cursor from result.nextCursor.

assertions.text: Response spreads the cursor into the request with a conditional spread.
Response reads the next cursor from nextCursor of the previous result.
Response does not assign a conditional object or undefined directly to cursors.
